---
title: "Advice or Enforcement"
---

::: {.quest-dialog}
**Prerequisites:** Plug In a Server, Guard the Door and the Rules of the Carapace. **Objective:** sort every control on this site by whether it advises, asks or enforces, and choose the right one for each risk.
**Time:** about 15 minutes. <span class="ao-badge">Last verified (docs, not run): Claude Code docs and OpenCode V2 docs on 2026-11-16 (sources in `research/tools-and-guards.md`)</span>
:::

Every control you have met does one of three things.

- **Advises.** It puts words in front of the model: an instructions file, Skill text, a line in your prompt. The model reads it and may weigh it against everything else in its context. Nothing stops a tool call.
- **Asks.** The harness pauses and puts the decision to you: a permission prompt, or an `ask` rule. It is only as good as your attention at the tenth prompt of the hour.
- **Enforces.** Code outside the model refuses the action whatever the model wants: a `deny` rule, a hook that exits 2, a sandbox where one is on. Enforcement has edges too, listed below.

The Gatehouse's rule of thumb: advice for preferences, a prompt for decisions you want to make each time, enforcement for things that must never happen.

## Each control, and its edge

::: {.panel-tabset group="companion"}

## Claude Code

| Control | Kind | Edge, per the docs read or earlier quests |
|---|---|---|
| `CLAUDE.md`, Skill text, your prompt | Advises | Influences the model only. |
| Permission prompt or `ask` rule | Asks | You must read it. A project `.mcp.json` server has its own approval prompt, and `-p` runs cannot show it. |
| `deny` rule | Enforces | Matching on command arguments is fragile (see the Carapace quest). Deny and ask rules are still evaluated when a hook returns allow. |
| `PreToolUse` hook, exit 2 | Enforces | Fires only on tool calls, sees the literal text, fails open if it crashes. |
| Sandbox | Enforces | Off by default, and limits shell commands only (see the Carapace quest). The docs say its restrictions still apply if a prompt injection bypasses the model's decision. |
| Git history | Recovers | Does not prevent anything. A commit is a restore point that exists whatever the model did next. |

A hook that **exits 0 with no JSON decision is not a control at all**: it expresses no decision and the normal permission flow runs. (A hook can also exit 0 and print a JSON `deny` decision, which does block.)

## OpenCode + Ollama

| Control | Kind | Edge, per the V2 docs read |
|---|---|---|
| Instructions file, Skill text, your prompt | Advises | Influences the model only. |
| Permission rule with effect `ask`; no matching rule | Asks | No match means `ask`. |
| Permission rule with effect `deny` | Enforces | An explicit configured `deny` is final and does not invoke the hook. |
| Plugin permission hook (`evaluate`) | Enforces when it denies | Runs for `allow` and `ask` decisions, and can change the effect to `deny`. |
| Git history | Recovers | Does not prevent anything. |

Not checked for OpenCode: an exit-code-2 equivalent, whether throwing in a tool hook blocks a call, sandboxing, and the effect of a local Ollama model. Check the current docs before counting on any of them.

:::

## Choose by the cost of being wrong

| Risk | Control | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Style: prefer `snake_case`, tidy commit messages | Advice | A miss costs a review comment. |
| Pushing to a shared branch | Ask | You want to decide each time, with context. |
| Reading `.env` or key files | Deny rule on the Read tool, plus sandbox or hook for Bash (enforce); still not total | It must never happen, so use enforcement, and cover each route the agent could use. |
| A specific destructive command you can name | Blocking hook (enforce) | Code refuses it. Accept that it covers only what it matches. |
| Fetched text telling the agent to act | Least privilege, read-only servers, sceptical reading | Advice may not hold against text the model has already read, so limit what the agent can do. |
| An experiment that might wreck your files | Git commit plus a scratch folder | Recovery, not prevention. |

Layer them: advice to steer, enforcement for the non-negotiable, git for the day something slips through. None of them replaces reading the diff.
